subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A 'storyboard' is most useful for planning...
options: A sequence such as an animation or advert
questions.explain: A storyboard sketches a sequence of frames to plan how an animation or film will unfold.

questions.q: In a composition, what is the 'focal point'?
options: The main area that draws the viewer's eye
The darkest area of the picture
questions.explain: The focal point is the part of the composition that attracts the viewer's attention first.

questions.q: In a repeating textile print, the single unit that repeats is called the...
questions.explain: The motif is the design unit that is repeated across the fabric to form an all-over pattern.

questions.q: 'Saturation' in an image describes...
options: The intensity or purity of the colours
questions.explain: Saturation measures how vivid or intense the colours are; low saturation looks washed out.

questions.q: 'White space' (negative space) in a layout is...
options: The empty areas that help organise and balance a design
A design fault to be avoided
questions.explain: White space is the empty area around elements that gives a layout clarity and balance.

questions.q: What is 'impasto' in painting?
options: Paint thinned to a watery wash
Thick paint applied so brush or knife marks stand out
Painting only in black and white
questions.explain: Impasto is thickly applied paint that leaves visible, textured marks on the surface.

questions.q: Which textile designer is famous for nature-inspired patterns of the Arts and Crafts movement?
questions.explain: William Morris designed richly patterned, nature-based textiles and wallpapers in the Arts and Crafts style.

questions.q: Which material is most suitable for bending into a flowing linear 3D form?
questions.explain: Wire is easily bent and twisted, making it ideal for linear, gestural 3D forms.

questions.q: 'Devore' (burnout) is a technique that...
options: Uses a chemical to dissolve fibres and leave a sheer pattern
questions.explain: Devore applies a chemical paste that burns away certain fibres, leaving a sheer patterned effect.

questions.q: Which is an example of three-dimensional design in everyday life?
options: A product such as a chair
questions.explain: Product design, such as a chair, is a form of three-dimensional design.

questions.q: 'Packaging' design must do all of these EXCEPT...
questions.explain: Packaging protects, informs and attracts, but it does not replace the product it contains.

questions.q: Shooting from a low viewpoint looking up tends to make a subject appear...
questions.explain: A low viewpoint looking up can make a subject seem larger, dominant or more imposing.

questions.q: Quilting involves...
options: Stitching layers of fabric together, often with wadding between them
questions.explain: Quilting sews together layers of cloth, usually with a padded wadding sandwiched between them.

questions.q: Which genre focuses on capturing real events and everyday life truthfully?
questions.explain: Documentary photography records real events, people and life as honestly as possible.

questions.q: 'Installation art' is best described as...
options: A small painting hung on a wall
A three-dimensional work that transforms a whole space for the viewer to enter
questions.explain: Installation art creates an immersive environment, often filling a space the viewer moves through.

questions.q: In GCSE Art, the assessment objective about 'recording' asks you to...
options: Write an essay with no images
Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to your intentions
questions.explain: The recording objective is about capturing observations and ideas, for example through drawing and photography.

questions.q: In film photography, in which room is light-sensitive paper developed?
questions.explain: Film and prints are processed in a darkroom, where safelight prevents the paper being fogged.

questions.q: The rule of thirds suggests you place key features where?
options: In the exact centre of the image
Along lines that divide the image into thirds or at their intersections
Around the edges of the frame
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the picture into a 3x3 grid and places focal points on the lines or intersections.

questions.q: Which drawing medium is best for soft, smudgeable, very dark marks?
questions.explain: Charcoal produces rich, dark, easily smudged marks ideal for tonal drawing.

questions.q: Appliqué is a technique that involves...
options: Stitching shaped pieces of fabric onto a larger background cloth
questions.explain: Appliqué sews cut pieces of fabric onto a background to build up an image or pattern.

questions.q: Jackson Pollock is famous for which technique?
options: Dripping and pouring paint onto canvas
questions.explain: Jackson Pollock developed a 'drip' technique, pouring paint onto canvas laid on the floor.

questions.q: Which method would a sculptor use to make a hollow form from sheet material?
options: Construction by folding and joining sheets
questions.explain: Folding and joining sheet material is a construction method that can create hollow 3D forms.
